notes: Same access/site background as bs154.json. The site's own top-level mega-menu carries a 'News' item (/en-int/collections/news, H1='News') - this is the English rendering of the Danish new-arrivals concept 'Nyheder' per the task brief's local-language equivalents, and functions exactly like a New Arrivals feed. Verified exact qty by exhaustive products.json pagination (limit=250): page 1 returned 123 unique product IDs (all vendor='House Doctor'), page 2 returned 0 - exhaustive, not the (possibly inflated) raw products_count field, consistent with Rule 1 from the prior Home-Decor pass for this company. A second nav item, 'AW26 Collection' (/en-int/collections/aw26-collection, the current season's marketing label), was checked and found to be a 100% product-ID-identical alias of 'News' (123/123 overlap, 0 unique to either side) - kept only the canonical 'News' row and dropped 'AW26 Collection' as a duplicate rollup, per the alias-merge rule. Also opened /en-int/pages/news-categories (linked as a 'Categories' index under News): its tiles (Home decor/Furniture/Outdoor/Kitchen accessories/Bathroom accessories/Home Office/Storage/Entrance/Home textiles) all link to the ordinary type-tree category pages (e.g. /collections/home-decor), NOT to any filtered/scoped New-Arrivals sub-collection - confirmed via live-browser link inspection - so this is just a navigational index page, not genuine New-Arrivals sub-structure; no per-category New Arrivals children exist. Checked header/footer/collections.json (271 collections) and Shopify search-suggest API for 'new in'/'just arrived'/'latest'/'newly added'/Danish 'nyt' - no other candidates found beyond News/AW26 Collection. Site search suggest for generic 'new' terms wasn't discriminating (matches too broadly on product titles), so absence of other New Arrivals pages was confirmed via direct nav/sitemap/collections.json enumeration instead, per the false-absence-test note.
